methods.label: Find the water cross section
methods.explanation:
The water has the same cross section along the tank's \(9\)-foot length, so first find its area in a circular end.

Let \(O\) be the circle's center, \(T\) its lowest point, and \(P,Q\) the endpoints of the horizontal water surface. Let \(M\) be where that surface meets the vertical radius \(OT\). Since \(OT=4\) and the water depth is \(MT=2\), we have \(OM=MT=2\).

Thus the line \(PQ\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(OT\), giving \(PT=PO=4\) and \(QT=QO=4\). Together with \(OT=4\), these equalities make triangles \(OPT\) and \(OQT\) equilateral. Each has a \(60^\circ\) angle at \(O\), so the sector containing the lower arc from \(P\) to \(Q\) has central angle \(120^\circ\).

The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
MP=MQ=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt3,
\]
so \(PQ=4\sqrt3\). The water region is the \(120^\circ\) sector with triangle \(OPQ\) removed. Its area is
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=\frac{120}{360}\pi(4^2)
-\frac12(4\sqrt3)(2)\\
&=\frac{16\pi}{3}-4\sqrt3.
\end{aligned}
\]
Multiplying this cross-sectional area by the tank's length gives
\[
V=9S=\boxed{48\pi-36\sqrt3}
\]
cubic feet, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
